name: Notability
tagline: iPad handwriting notebook with Apple Pencil ink, PDF markup and audio recording tied to your notes.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is less magical than it looks, because Apple already gives you the hard part: PencilKit does low-latency ink, palm rejection and an eraser, and PDFKit does document annotation. An agent can absolutely produce a working iPad notebook app in a weekend that captures handwriting on scrolling pages, imports PDFs to mark up, and records audio with timestamps you can tap back into. The gaps are all the boring infrastructure: you need a Mac, Xcode, and a signing profile, and a free provisioning profile expires every seven days unless you pay for a developer account. Sync across devices, handwriting search, lasso-to-move, shape straightening and the sheer feel of a mature ink engine are where the remaining year of work lives. Fine as a personal notebook, annoying as the only place your lecture notes live.
coreLoopDIY: A local iPad app that captures Apple Pencil ink on infinite-scroll pages, annotates imported PDFs, and records audio with timestamps that jump back to what you were writing at that moment.
requirements: an Apple ID for signing, ideally a paid developer account so the build does not expire weekly
whatYouLose: Cross-device sync and backup, so your notebooks live on one iPad until you build export
Handwriting recognition and search inside ink, which is the feature people actually rely on months later
Mature ink polish: lasso select, shape straightening, pressure curves, undo that never glitches
Broad import and export compatibility with the note formats classmates and coworkers send you
Years of existing notebooks, which do not come with you
moatNotes: PencilKit hands you the technically scary part, so the real moat is a decade of small interaction decisions plus the archive of notebooks you already made.
whyPeopleStillPay: Handwriting apps are used daily, in classes and meetings, under time pressure, and any friction is unacceptable. A single dropped stroke, a laggy scroll, or a note that failed to sync before a lecture ends is worse than the subscription price. Notability also holds people's back catalog, and nobody re-inks four semesters of notes to escape a yearly fee. A DIY build is a great second notebook and a bad only notebook.
notes: The ink engine is free from Apple; the trust that your notes will still be there in March is not.
prompt:
Build a personal iPad handwriting notebook app. Native only, no web app, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack: Swift, SwiftUI, PencilKit, PDFKit, AVFoundation. Target iPadOS 17 or later. Create a fresh Xcode project named InkPad with a single app target. No third-party packages.

Data model, stored on device only:
- A Notebook has a title, created and modified dates, and an ordered list of Pages.
- A Page stores a PKDrawing as Data, plus an optional background: blank, ruled, grid, or a page of an imported PDF.
- Persist each notebook as a folder in the app's Documents directory: metadata.json plus one .drawing file per page, plus source.pdf and audio.m4a when present. No Core Data, no CloudKit.

Screens:
1. Library: grid of notebooks with title and modified date, a plus button to create one, swipe to delete, long press to rename.
2. Editor: vertically scrolling pages, each a PKCanvasView sized to US Letter aspect ratio, drawing enabled with allowsFingerDrawing off. Show the standard PKToolPicker. A toolbar has undo, redo, add page, page background picker, and share.
3. PDF import: a file importer that takes a PDF, renders each page as the Page background via PDFKit, and lets ink land on top.

Audio: a record button in the editor toolbar records to audio.m4a and writes a JSON sidecar of stroke timestamps, mapping wall-clock offsets to page index. During playback, show a scrub bar and highlight which page was active at that moment. Simple is fine, do not attempt per-stroke replay animation.

Export: share sheet exporting a flattened PDF of the notebook, ink composited over backgrounds via UIGraphicsPDFRenderer.

Explicitly out of scope: sync, handwriting recognition or search inside ink, shape straightening, lasso transform, collaboration, tags, OCR, any network calls. Do not add a login screen. No secrets are needed, so do not create a .env.

When done, print exact steps to open the project in Xcode, select an iPad target, sign with a personal team, and run on device, including the warning that a free provisioning profile expires after seven days.
